desc: Ideation; refuted cycle-only hypothesis (star swaps in 6). Established: feasible ⇔ graph is not a simple path; answer = min-length schedulable closed walk C = W_A ++ W_B with a valid split point (A pauses at x: first part avoids T, B's route avoids x, last part avoids S).
Hand-derived candidate formula and verified on ~10 hand-built cases (star, star-center, path+branch, branch-behind-S, lollipop=10, dumbbell=8, triangle-leaf=5 via cycle-through-S, samples 1–3).

Brute-force BFS over ordered pairs for N≤7; enumerate small connected graphs; ground-truth generator with sharding, gzip, validate() helper; in-memory smoke enumerator for n≤6 with candidate_predict() and mismatch bucketing.

Validate and correct candidate formula vs brute force on n≤6: pinned branch coefficients (+2 internal / +4 endpoint), replaced constant off-path +4 with distance-dependent cost, confirmed cycle-through-S/T terms, ruled out exotic cheaper structures; full shard n=2..6 converged to checked=1632322 mismatches=0.

Design efficient computation of the corrected formula: BFS from S and T; scan degree≥3 vertices for branch costs (with correct distance terms); shortest cycle through a pair via node-split min-cost flow (2 units, cap-1 vertices, no spurious 2-cycles, forced same-u convergence) or block-cut-based alternative; prove no underestimation; prove normal-form lemma (one passing gadget, one hide).
Implement final O((N+M) log N) solution: BFS from S,T; branch scan; the two flow/cycle computations; answer = min over gadgets else -1. Careful 1-indexing, N=2, adjacent S,T, path-graph → -1.
Cross-validate final solution against brute force on all small graphs (sharded n=7 runs, merge counts) and random small graphs; check samples 1–3.
